title: Praise the LORD, All You Nations

verses.text: Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol Him, all you peoples!
For great is His loving devotion toward us, and the faithfulness of the LORD endures forever. Hallelujah!

context.author: Not named. The shortest psalm and the shortest chapter in the Bible, sung as part of the Hallel.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: Two verses, and the whole world is invited: “Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol Him, all you peoples!” (v.1). The reason is what God has done for Israel: “For great is His loving devotion toward us, and the faithfulness of the LORD endures forever. Hallelujah!” (v.2). God’s faithfulness to one people becomes good news for every people.
context.custom: In its two verses the psalm has the two great words of God’s character, chesed (loving devotion) and emet (faithfulness), the pair God proclaimed at Sinai (Exodus 34:6). It was sung after the Passover meal as part of the Hallel.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 118 closes the Hallel: the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
context.timelineBible: Paul quotes v.1 to show that God always meant to save the nations: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples” (Romans 15:11). Jesus sent His disciples to “make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19).

translation.meaning: To praise; the root of Hallelujah.

gospelParallels.note: Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles.

overview.summary: The shortest psalm calls every nation to praise the LORD for His great love and faithfulness to Israel, which endure forever.
overview.settingLine: Two verses for the whole world.

archaeology.t: Copies from Qumran show the Hallel psalms were sung and copied together.
Later synagogue mosaics and inscriptions in Israel quote psalms of praise.

overview.discussion: God’s faithfulness to Israel is a reason for all nations to praise (v.2). How does God’s faithfulness to others give me reason to praise Him?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Not named
